channel.title: Wire — Programming
channel.description: Programming from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
item.description: We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms. (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
item.description: The experiments that read raw weights and the ones that fix Qwen use completely different techniques. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: A Decade of Kill Bugs – Alan Grow
item.description: … A bug in kill was so surprising that, once I'd found it, I couldn't stop there. I needed to know how this bug came to be, and what had led the programmers so badly astray. (2 sources: lobsters, rprogramming)

item.title: Could a modern chess engine on a Pentium have defeated Kasparov in 1996?
item.description: A fun experiment where I back-port all the improvements we've made to chess engines over the last 30 years and run it on a 1996 Pentium Pro to see what we could have done if only we knew more at the time. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Nvidia – open-source auto-ontology
item.description: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Show HN: Hacker Times, a New York Times-inspired version of Hacker News
item.description: A newspaper from Hacker News, refreshed every hour. Independent headlines, original sources. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Designing a planned switchover for minimum disruption
item.description: How Neki uses preflight checks, query buffering, synchronous replication, and fast rollback to make Postgres primary switchovers less disruptive. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Why did you choose the nix you nix?
item.description: I don't which nix is good and at this point I'm afraid I need to ask. (Cpp) Nix Determinate Nix Lix Or, you know, Guix ? (I suspect that Snix , Tvix , and others aren't intended for general use… but I might be wrong?) (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: I made a game in 3 kB… and accidentally created a programming language
item.description: I wrote a technical blog post about my experimentation a few months ago. I've just adapted the content to youtube, so you can choose the format you enjoy the most:… (1 source: rprogramming)
